meta.purpose: Research findings for building an MCP server to expose knowledge base search tools

fastmcp_api.history: FastMCP 1.0 was incorporated into official MCP Python SDK in 2024. FastMCP 2.0 added resources/prompts. FastMCP 3.0 (2026-01-19) added component versioning, granular auth, OpenTelemetry. 3.1.0 is latest.
fastmcp_api.note_on_mcp_sdk: The official 'mcp' PyPI package (modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk) also includes a built-in FastMCP class. For simple servers, either package works. The standalone 'fastmcp' package has more advanced features (proxying, composition, etc).

core_pattern.description: Create a FastMCP instance, decorate functions with @mcp.tool, call mcp.run()

key_features: Type hints auto-generate JSON schema for tool parameters
Pydantic model support for complex inputs/outputs
Both sync and async functions supported
Return types: str, dict, list, Pydantic models all handled automatically
fastmcp_api.async_support: Built-in. Use 'async def' for I/O-bound operations like database queries. FastMCP handles both sync and async transparently.
fastmcp_api.context_parameter: Inject Context object for logging, progress reporting: 'async def my_tool(query: str, ctx: Context) -> str'

transport_options.summary: Three transport types exist. stdio is best for Claude Code local servers. Streamable HTTP for remote. SSE is deprecated.

stdio.description: Server runs as a local subprocess. Communication over stdin/stdout.
stdio.best_for: Local tools, CLI integration, Claude Code

streamable_http.description: HTTP POST/GET with optional SSE streaming. Introduced in MCP spec 2025-03-26.
cons: Known issues with long-running streaming tools in Claude Code
streamable_http.claude_code_usage: claude mcp add --transport http my-server https://host:port/mcp

sse.description: Server-Sent Events over HTTP. DEPRECATED as of MCP spec 2025-03-26.
sse.claude_code_usage: claude mcp add --transport sse my-server https://host:port/sse

transport_options.recommendation_for_this_project: Use stdio. The KB MCP server will run locally alongside Claude Code. stdio is the default, simplest, and most reliable transport. No network setup needed.

local_scope.description: Default. Private to you, current project only.

project_scope.description: Shared with team. Claude Code prompts for approval on first use.
project_scope.how_to_add: claude mcp add --scope project my-server -- python /path/to/server.py

user_scope.description: Available across all projects for this user.
user_scope.how_to_add: claude mcp add --scope user my-server -- python /path/to/server.py

notes: command should be absolute path or in PATH
Claude Code prompts for approval before using project-scoped servers

claude_code_config.verification: Use /mcp command inside Claude Code to check server status
claude_code_config.timeout: Set MCP_TIMEOUT env var for startup timeout (e.g., MCP_TIMEOUT=10000)

minimal_server_design.description: Minimal viable MCP server wrapping the existing SQLite FTS5 knowledge base with search/get/list tools

tools.name: kb_search
tools.description: Full-text search the knowledge base using FTS5 with BM25 ranking

parameters.resource_type: str | None - filter by type (KB, SOP, SRC, SCR, TEAM, TOOL)

tools.returns: list of {id, title, resource_type, summary, score}

tools.name: kb_get
tools.description: Read a specific knowledge base entry by ID

parameters.fields: str | None - comma-separated fields to return

tools.returns: dict with entry fields, tags, and relationships

tools.name: kb_list
tools.description: List all entries of a given resource type

parameters.resource_type: str - KB, SOP, SRC, SCR, TEAM, or TOOL

tools.name: kb_tags
tools.description: Get tag frequency cloud, optionally filtered by resource type

tools.name: kb_related
tools.description: Find entries related to a given entry via builds_on and shared tags

parameters.entry_id: str - entry ID to find relationships for

architecture_notes: Reuse existing query_kb.py logic - import or copy the SQL queries
Connect to storage/data/knowledge.db with WAL mode
All tools return JSON-serializable dicts (FastMCP handles serialization)
Use async def for database operations where possible
Error handling: return descriptive error messages, not exceptions
minimal_server_design.pseudocode:
from fastmcp import FastMCP
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

mcp = FastMCP("Knowledge Base Search")
DB = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data" / "knowledge.db"

def get_db():
    db = sqlite3.connect(str(DB))
    db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    db.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
    return db

@mcp.tool
def kb_search(query: str, resource_type: str = None, limit: int = 10) -> list[dict]:
    """Search the knowledge base using full-text search with BM25 ranking."""

    return results

@mcp.tool
def kb_get(entry_id: str, fields: str = None) -> dict:
    """Read a specific knowledge base entry by ID (e.g., KB-0034)."""
    db = get_db()
    # ... read query from query_kb.py ...
    return entry

@mcp.tool
def kb_list(resource_type: str = "KB") -> list[dict]:
    """List all entries of a given type (KB, SOP, SRC, SCR, TEAM, TOOL)."""
    db = get_db()
    # ... list query from query_kb.py ...
    return entries

@mcp.tool
def kb_tags(resource_type: str = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Get tag frequency cloud for the knowledge base."""
    db = get_db()
    # ... tags query from query_kb.py ...
    return tags

@mcp.tool
def kb_related(entry_id: str) -> dict:

    db = get_db()
    # ... related query from query_kb.py ...
    return related

if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()

tools_vs_resources.summary: Both can be exposed from the same MCP server. For our use case, tools are the right choice for search/get operations because Claude needs to decide when to search.

tools.control: Model-driven - the LLM decides when to invoke them
tools.purpose: Execute actions, perform computation, query data
tools.side_effects: Can modify state (but read-only is fine too)
tools.analogy: Like POST/PUT endpoints in a REST API
tools.invocation: LLM autonomously calls based on context
tools.client_support: Universally supported by all MCP clients

resources.control: Application-driven - the host app decides when to load them
resources.analogy: Like GET endpoints in a REST API
resources.invocation: User/app decides via @ mentions in Claude Code (e.g., @kb:entry://KB-0034)
resources.client_support: Only 26 of 58 MCP clients support resources
resources.claude_code_support: Yes - resources appear in @ mention autocomplete

recommendation.primary: Use tools for all search/get/list operations - Claude needs autonomous access to query the KB during problem-solving
recommendation.optional_resources: Optionally expose individual KB entries as resources (e.g., kb://entry/KB-0034) for direct @ mention reference, but this is lower priority
recommendation.rationale: Tools are model-controlled (Claude decides when to search), which is exactly what we want. Resources require the user to explicitly reference them, which adds friction.

recommended_approach.summary: Build a single-file FastMCP server (~50 lines) that wraps the existing SQLite FTS5 database, expose 5 tools (search, get, list, tags, related), configure via .mcp.json at repo root for project-wide access.

steps.notes: Single dependency. Alternatively 'pip install fastmcp' or 'pip install mcp' (official SDK includes FastMCP)

steps.details: Single file, ~50 lines. Import FastMCP, connect to knowledge.db, define 5 tools wrapping the SQL queries from query_kb.py. All tools return JSON-serializable dicts.

commands: Ask Claude: 'Search the knowledge base for MCP'

steps.action: Optional: Add resources for direct entry access
steps.details: Add @mcp.resource decorators for kb://entry/{id} patterns so users can @ mention specific entries

key_decisions.package: fastmcp (standalone) or mcp (official SDK) - both work, fastmcp has more features
key_decisions.transport: stdio (local, simple, default for Claude Code)
key_decisions.tools_not_resources: Tools for search/query (model-controlled), optional resources later
key_decisions.database: Reuse existing storage/data/knowledge.db with WAL mode
